category_title: Students with autism exhibiting sensory-maintained skin scratching
minimal_context: Tommy is completing his math work while seated at a table in close proximity to his peers in the mild/moderate special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your math work for today. Please sit at this table next to your classmates and complete the assignment.

STUDENT: (Begins completing his work and simultaneously scratches his own skin) Okay.

TUTOR: Keep going with the math problems.

STUDENT: I am feeling nervous. Scratching feels good and helps calm me down.

TUTOR: Just try your best to finish the page.

STUDENT: (Reaches over to the student sitting next to him, grabs the peer’s hand, and uses it to scratch his own skin)

options.A: Allow the student to work at his own pace and take breaks when desired.
options.B: Prompt the student to use the stress-relief ball if he begins scratching.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each math task during the period.
options.D: Provide a range of different math activities within the class period.
